correctness.rationale: For each simple residue root the Hensel lift α is unique and the factor f(x)/(x−α) is a unit on its root disk. Thus outside the root disks the valuation is zero, and within one it measures agreement with its centre. Different residue disks are disjoint. Two balls at depths t,s intersect exactly when their centres agree through min(t,s); then the intersection is the deeper ball and contains p^{k−max(t,s)} residues modulo p^k. This gives both exact finite tails and the stated Haar tails. In the mixed tail series the diagonal at m=min(t,s) contributes (zw)^{m−1}p^{−m}; the two off-diagonals multiply this by z/(p−z) and w/(p−w). Geometric summation over m≤d yields the PGF, with no convergence problem on the closed unit bidisk even at d=∞. At z=w=1 the mixed-tail sum is (p+1)Σ(1−p^{−d_a})/(p−1)^2. Subtracting the marginal product gives the formula. For split quadratics, r=0 is negative and r=2 is positive even at minimal d=1. For r=1 the numerator is −4·3^{−d} at p=3 and at least (p²−4p−1)/p>0 for p≥5. Coinciding lifts as well as empty root sets are consistent with the formulas in RESULT.md.
residual_risks: The replay compares four full truncated PMFs, at (p,k)=(3,6) twice, (5,5), and (7,4), including finite and infinite collision depths. A truncated covariance need not have the sign of the limiting covariance, notably when the latter is zero. The exact general result uses the proof, not these histograms.

Read the slogan's dependency shorthand with r_f and r_g held fixed: the list of common-root depths alone does not determine marginal distributions. The actual theorem includes both counts. No claim is validated for nonsimple residue roots.

evidence: The weighted-tree formula allows arbitrary distinct integral p-adic residues of rational roots and arbitrary positive root multiplicities, including the case of a merged root with combined multiplicity. Snyder's Theorem 5.2 records the first differing digit per rational linear factor, then adds them. Bories instead treats polynomial maps under a strong nondegeneracy hypothesis.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The restriction to rational centres in the weighted-tree theorem does not obstruct this application. Replace each polynomial by the product of the linear factors at its simple p-adic lifts, with valuation unaffected since all other factors are units locally. Choose k greater than every finite pairwise collision depth. Replace each distinct centre by an integer representative of its class modulo p^k, using the same representative for actual coincidences. Translate each occupied p^k-disk from its lift to that representative, leaving other disks fixed. This bijection preserves Haar and preserves every valuation to the corresponding centres: within that disk the intended difference is invariant, and any difference to an outside centre has valuation less than k. Thus the prior rational-root theorem applies to exactly the same joint law, not just to the rationally split examples in the record.

evidence: At a tree vertex the prior W(u) is the sum of multiplicities sharing the prefix, and W*(B_u) is the cumulative sum on its stalk. For F^mG^n, every nonzero W is at least 2 when m,n≥2. The prior internal vertex term is p^{−1−level}(p−valence)T^{W*}; the terminal term is (1−p^{−1})p^{−level}T^{W*}/(1−p^{−1}T^W). Under z=T^m,w=T^n each monomial separates by the two colours.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In this specialization a singly occupied residue has one colour path; a common residue has both colours until depth d, then one path of each colour (or stays common for coincident centres). The prior terms give mass (p−1)/p^{j+1} on (j,j) for 1≤j<d, (p−2)/p^{d+1} on (d,d) at the split, and (p−1)/p^{j+1} on each of (j,d),(d,j) for j>d. With d=∞ the unbranched diagonal continues forever. These terms and the single-colour geometric marginals already give the joint law, its coefficients and the finite counts by reduction. The covariance is their first mixed moment minus the product of marginals; for quadratics the sign takes a three-case substitution in the resulting expression. The additional sign labels do not require an independent structural theorem.

evidence: The PGF is the independently weighted local integral of |f|_p^{s_1}|g|_p^{s_2}. Bories's mapping zeta applies a norm and encodes min(X,Y), not that integral. Zúñiga-Galindo's scalar integral, in contrast, can be taken on F^mG^n for all m,n. The local ternary-cumulant record states the same covariance on two matched roots at equal finite depth, but has the same date as the target and does not establish priority.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A single product valuation only gives X+Y, but arbitrary multiplicities recover independent coordinate weights. For fixed 0<T<1 the integrals of F^mG^n give the pair PGF at (T^m,T^n) for independently varying m,n≥2; the analytic identity principle in each variable then determines it. More strongly the prior tree formula explicitly gives those two weights in its monomials, not just uniqueness from sampled values.

originality.rationale: There is positive prior-implication evidence, not merely a search limitation. Zúñiga-Galindo's explicit weighted root-tree generating function (math/0204360v1, §§4–5, notably Lemma 5.1) covers the bivariate law by assigning multiplicities m,n to the two factors of a rationally split product. The transfer to arbitrary simple Hensel lifts needs only disjoint translations of sufficiently deep residue disks, not a new zeta-function calculation. Its explicit vertex terms specialize to the two-colour shell law, and the covariance and quadratic sign alternatives are direct summation and comparison of those terms. The frozen comparison considers product sums at fixed weights, not this arbitrary-multiplicity reduction. The stronger prior need not state the specific covariance wording.
residual_risks: No assertion that the exact bivariate wording or the significance of p=3 was stated earlier. The negative judgment is based on a specific implication from an earlier explicit generating theorem; the targeted searches are not exhaustive.

value.rationale: The dependence question is natural and the sign description is useful exposition, but this exact law is mechanically supplied by the pre-existing explicit weighted-tree evaluation: the specialization has only single-colour stalks and at most one bifurcation per residue. The proposed additional boundary is a geometric moment sum and substitution of r=0,1,2 into that same known law. No independent non-routine unknown exact fact is established beyond this specialization; the finite check and alternate proof add neither.
residual_risks: This is not a judgment against studying sign phenomena for more general joint valuations, and it does not reject the mathematical formulas as false. No changed claim has been assessed as a repair.
